# A Second Kind of Pulley Problem

<!-- STEP id="the-setup" -->
A 4 kg block sits on a frictionless table.

A string ties it to a 2 kg block hanging off the edge, over a smooth pulley fixed at the corner.

Let go, and the hanging block falls — dragging the table block sideways.

<!-- STEP id="table-block-fbd" -->
## The Table Block's Diagram

Three forces act on it: weight down, normal force up, tension sideways.

Weight and normal force cancel vertically — the same balance you met two lessons ago.

Tension is the only force with anything left to do:

$$T = m_1a$$

<!-- STEP id="hanging-block-fbd" -->
## The Hanging Block's Diagram

Two forces act on it: weight down, tension up.

It's the one actually falling, so 'down' is positive for it.

$$m_2g - T = m_2a$$

<!-- STEP id="combine" -->
## Adding the Two Equations

$T$ cancels again.

$$a = \frac{m_2g}{m_1 + m_2}$$

<!-- STEP id="whats-different" -->
## What Changed

Only the hanging block's weight drives the motion.

The table block adds mass — inertia to overcome — but no weight to the pulling side. The table already canceled its weight with the normal force.

**Same method, different free-body diagrams, because the setup is different.**
